messages.subject: Error in Part 1
parts:
Hi,

I am receiving this error when trying to run the first part of GGIR

Errors and warnings for LAB_2023_020100074_T0_058642_2023-07-15 10-11-27.csv$message
[1] "'to' must be of length 1"

$call
seq.default(rawTime[1], rawTime[length(rawTime)], step)

And the same error is provided for every .csv file that GGIR tries to analyse within the working directory. I'm not too sure what it is referring to, and I can only imagine it's the timestamp, which goes up by 1 second every row.

Here is my code for context:

GGIR(mode =c(1,2,3,4,5),
     datadir="/Users/georgeannas/Desktop/CPC Research/Data/FALAH School 1 No Column",
     outputdir="/Users/georgeannas/Desktop/CPC Research/Data/FALAH Data",

                    rmc.unit.acc = "g",
                    rmc.col.time = 1,
                    rmc.dec = ".",
                    rmc.unit.time = "character",
                    rmc.firstrow.acc = 2,
                    rmc.col.acc = 2:4,
                    rmc.col.temp = 6,
                    rmc.unit.temp = "C",
                    rmc.format.time = "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S",
                    desiredtz = "Australia/Sydney"))

Thanks for the help guys!

Hi Vincent,

I've just reread your message now. I created a new R script just testing if the read.myacc.csv function could read my files and I discovered 2 issues.

1). Even though I was specifying the timestamp column, GGIR was extracting the date from the ID column at the very end thus causing confusing timestamp extractions:
          time           x            y            z temperature
1   1686852000 -0.94725596 -0.355413504  0.147980003           0
2   1686852001 -0.95017586 -0.354148355  0.149060938           0
3   1686852002 -0.94659234 -0.361273139  0.146088366           0
4   1686852003 -0.94864955 -0.361073379  0.150817457           0

also see how the temperature column is empty even though it is most definitely populated (it may be reading the light column even though I have specified the column number for temperature as well)

2) After removing the ID column, I get this error from running the read.myacc.csv function on its own:
Extraction of timestamps unsuccesful, check timestamp format arguments

I believe I have specified the right format arguments so I am confused now as to why this error seems to be occuring. Please see my updated standalone read.myacc.csv function here:
library(GGIR)

rmc.unit.acc = "g",
  rmc.unit.temp = "C",
  rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",
  rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
  desiredtz = "Pacific/Noumea",
  rmc.sf = 1
)

Thanks Vincent!

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in Part 1
parts:
Hi George,

When I look at the example file in a text editor I see that raw data is:

timestamp,xm,ym,zm,lightm,tempm,svmgsum,sdx,sdy,sdz,id
15/6/2023 18:00,-0.947255956,....

The timestamp shows only hours and minutes but no seconds. I suspect Excel did that while you saved a copy of the file. Be mindful that Excel likes to fiddle with data when it is re-saved. As a result, I cannot test your code.

Additionally, I see the timestamp format in your raw file is day/month/year and not year-month-date. Open the file in a text editor to check timestamp format.

Another problem I see is that you are referring to the top line as the file header. The top line are column headers but not the file header, your file does not have a file header so you can set:
rmc.firstrow.header = c(),
rmc.header.length = c(),

I see that the last column indicates .bin What accelerometer brand are you working with? If it is GENEActiv then why not work with the .bin files directly?

Re. removal of ID column: There should not be any reason to delete columns from files that are not used.

Timestamps in output of function read.myacc.csv are always expressed in seconds since 1-1-1970. I now see I did not document that.

Thanks,

Vincent
